source_validation.scope: source geometry, contacts and explicit opening hosts

assumptions: Correction cell rings represent physical source spaces with horizontal floor/ceiling boundaries.
Contacts describe adjacency, not traversability or EnergyPlus surface pairing.
Only explicit openings are represented; absent observations do not establish a solid wall.
Source boundary identity follows cell identity and ring order; topology edits need identity migration.
Wall representative plane = measured pixel line centrelines/outer faces from pixel_profile scans, not nominal 240mm offsets.

Exterior opening heights this run are re-derived per facade from each elevation's own explicit dimension-chain labels, cross-checked by direct pixel measurement of wall-top/ground datums and the opening graphics themselves, rather than copied across facades.
North entrance door ND1 and South door SD1: z=[0.2,2.6]m, confirmed by strong pixel-to-label match (1900/2400/200 chain) on each facade independently.

East door ED1: z=[0.2,2.6]m assigned by close pixel-graphic match to the same door family as North/South (no separate adjacent explicit label found; the nearby 1100/2400/1000 label was determined to belong to the adjacent EW1 window instead, confirmed by a much closer pixel match to EW1's own graphic). This remains a documented inference, flagged in unresolved.

North window NW1 z=[1.0,3.4]; South windows SW1/SW2 z=[1.0,2.8]; East large window EW1 z=[1.0,3.4] (own 1100/2400/1000 chain, confirmed by close pixel match); East small windows EW2/EW3 z=[1.0,2.8] (EW3 confirmed via its own adjacent 1700/1800/1000 chain; EW2 assumed same small-window family, approximate pixel match).

West small windows WW1-WW4 z=[1.0,2.8]m: CORRECTED this run from the inherited assumption of matching North (1.0/3.4). West_view.png's own left-side chain (1700/1800/1000) is the only dimension evidence for these repeated openings and matches the South-window family instead.
West large boardroom window WW5 z=[1.0,3.4]m: unchanged; confirmed via West_view.png's own right-side chain (1100/2400/1000) adjacent to that specific window.

All interior (non-exterior) doors (D_lobby_corr, D_w2_corr, D_w3_corr, D_w4_corr, D_e2_corr, D_e3_corr, D_SE_divider) retain the prior explicit assumption z=[0,2.4]m: no elevation drawing shows interior partition door heights, so this remains an assumption, not independently re-verified this run (no conflicting evidence found).
Building height 4.5m used uniformly as the single floor's wall height per all four elevations (unchanged).

SE divider P7 and RoomSE_south partition/room findings from the prior run are preserved unchanged (out of this run's scope, which is limited to exterior opening z-intervals and supporting evidence/notes).

unresolved: ED1_door's z=[0.2,2.6] is inferred from pixel-graphic family matching, not an explicit adjacent dimension label on East_view.png; if a label was missed elsewhere on that facade, this should be re-checked.
EW2_window's z=[1.0,2.8] is assigned by visual/family similarity to EW3 and the small-window pattern; no explicit dimension chain was found directly adjacent to EW2 itself.

SW2_window's z=[1.0,2.8] is assumed identical to SW1 by facade symmetry; its own adjacent dimension chain was not independently re-confirmed by pixel measurement this run (South_view crop for SW2 was inconclusive due to a boundary/crop issue).
Interior door heights remain an unverified explicit assumption (2.4m, base 0); no drawing evidence confirms or contradicts this.
RoomSE_south's precise use/role remains unlabelled/uncertain (carried over from prior run, out of this run's scope).

Fine sub-dimension chain reconciliation across all four facades was not exhaustively re-summed beyond the specific opening chains checked this run; outer-bracket/pixel-measured boundaries continue to be trusted where checked.

scope.actual_openings: only explicit built source openings are inventoried

current_source_projections.basis: x anchors: left exterior wall outer face pixel 246 = world x0m; right exterior wall outer face pixel 612 = world x10m (matches 10000mm overall width dimension). y anchors: top exterior wall outer face pixel 150 = world y0m; bottom exterior wall outer face pixel 870 = world y20m (matches 20000mm overall height dimension). Plan y increases downward/south in image, matching drawing's own top-to-bottom dimension chain.

calibration_warnings.guidance: x=36.6 px/m and y=36 px/m disagree by 1.652893%, over the 0.300000% limit — at least one endpoint pair or transcribed dimension is likely wrong. Do not silently trust the blended px_per_m below: re-crop and re-measure both axes' anchors at their dimension-chain extension-line intersections, then recalibrate. If you must proceed now, prefer the single-axis scale (axis_px_per_m) for geometry measured along that axis over the blended value, and record this disagreement instead of treating the reading as clean.

scope.endpoint_selection: exact original image name and linked wall floor

limits: Endpoint pixels are the declared original-image evidence and are drawn without inferred movement.
Tangential range and normal displacement are conditional on the caller-supplied axis-aligned calibration.
A dimension extension-line tick may legitimately lie outside its linked finite wall segment; this is a spatial fact, not an error or correctness verdict.
This view does not inspect pixels, choose a host wall, or mutate source geometry or evidence.
